CITY OF INGLEWOOD

  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
September 7, 2022 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood Planning Commission will be
conducted pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e), which
allows the City to use teleconferencing for members of the public to access
a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in option.

CALL-IN OPTION
1. Members of the public who wish to attend the Planning Commission Meeting
of September 7, 2022 and address the Planning Commission must use the call-
in option noted below:
Instructions: Dial one of the Phone Numbers below and when prompted,
enter the Access Code:
  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 8239225#
In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the
meeting to the public using the call-in option, or in the event of a
disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering
public comments using the call-in option, the Planning Commission shall take
no further action on items appearing on the meeting agenda until public
access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to
submit comments and/or to observe a public meeting. The following
alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience
only and the disruption in service to any alternative method does not
preclude the Planning Commission from taking further action on an agenda
item. In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below members
of the public should use the call-in option above.
2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may
choose to submit comments for consideration by the Planning Commission by
sending  them  to  Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the
Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda, comments must be
received prior to 12:00 P.M. on the day of the meeting. Correspondence
should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after
12:00 P.M. and prior to the close of the public hearing will be made part
of the official public record of the meeting.
3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check
  with your cable provider for details
  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-5230,
One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California 90301.  All
requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to the day of
the hearing.
Español: "Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor
de llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

[Agenda Items and Additional Public Access Options Listed on Following Pages]
  1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

 2.  Roll Call.

 3.  Communications from staff.

 4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to address the
  Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other than a public
  hearing may do so at this time.

 5.  Minutes approval for August 3, 2022, Planning Commission meetings.

 6.  NON - PUBLIC HEARING:
  a. Overview report on Accessory Dwelling Units
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Receive and file Staff Memo
  2) Provide comments for future Ordinance
  Item 6a documents

 7.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning Commission on
  any matter within their jurisdiction and not elsewhere considered on
  the agenda may do so at this time.

 8.  Commission Initiatives.

 9.  Adjournment.

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of August 3, 2022, is not
held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other agenda item being
considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing agenda item will
automatically be continued to the next regular Planning Commission meeting.

Hearing materials are available at:

  and at City
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-4
Hall, 1st Floor Lobby Information Desk during regular business hours. If
any additional documents are received for distribution to the Planning
Commission after the publication of this Agenda but before 12:00 P.M. on

https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-4.

(Note: The above procedures are subject to change for future Commission

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 7, 2022

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, September 7, 2022, in the City
Council Chambers, on the ninth floor, of City Hall. Following the
Pledge of Allegiance by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, the meeting
was called to order at 7:01 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Absent:  Commissioner David Rice

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Christopher E. Jackson, ECD Director
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Mindy Wilcox, Planning Manager, stated there were none.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:

Chairman Springs called for a vote to approve August 3, 2022
minutes.

Motion to Approve August 3, 2022 Minutes by Commissioner Trejo and
seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Trejo, Shaw-Williams
Abstained:  Chairman Springs.

(6) NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A. OVERVIEW REPORT ON ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS:

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
 The State has already set guidelines of what they want and now
  each individual City must make some changes and adopt the States
  requirements of what the State has already set going forward?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 7, 2022

  This seems that the State has removed all freedom from the
  Cities in making their own decisions regarding ADU’s and JADU’s
  and the lack of space in the City.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  This is just a statement regarding where the Planning Commission
  went as a group to the last PC Conference and ADU’s were a
  subject there and how not all being on board with accepting
  ADU’s, with that being said, has our City been already accepting
  ADU requests and allowing them to be built?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  As Planning Commission says that we would like to require more
  parking spaces than what is allowed by the State, what happens
  with previous ADU builds if the City sets new standards?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  What other issues involved in allowing ADU’s, could it be
  setback issues, or lot sizes of the ADU’s or even parking
  problems?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff –
 Do we as the Planning Commission get to put some type of
  restrictions on parking issues that these ADU’s are causing?
   Mr. C. E. Jackson, ECD Director responded to Commissioner
  Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated to staff–
 Thanked staff for explaining our limitations as to what we would
  be able to allow with regards to an ADU, no further questions.

Commissioner Trejo stated to staff –
 One of the main concerns is ADU’s being turned into short-term
  rentals, and how they will not be turned into that type of use,
  and how will we be able to monitor this type of use?
 Also, the size of the ADU’s and JADU’s are an issue.
 Last, not enough parking once the ADU’s are added with
  regulating that issue.
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
   Mr. Pan, Assistant City Attorney responded to Commissioner
  Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs stated to staff –
 The State has taken it upon themselves to make these
  determinations for the state, but did not take it into
  consideration regarding this City’s size?
 Height is an issue, what about the setbacks for these ADU’s and
  JADU’s if they make second-story ADU’s they will be able to look
  directly into people’s backyard and into their home, because
  there are no height restrictions.
 The State took it upon themselves to force upon these Cities to
  approve their actions when the people of this state voted NO on
  having ADU’s, as I know for sure that no one including myself
  received anything from our state representatives about going
  against what we the people had already decided.
   Mr. Jackson responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 7, 2022
Commissioner Trejo stated to staff –
 That she is in agreement with Chairman Springs in not feeling
  good about the States decision, but she feels that it is upon
  the Planning Commission to come up with State approved
  restrictions, even if possibly having stronger restrictions with
  regards to setbacks and solutions for those who apply for ADU &
  JADU applications going forward.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s statement.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
 Is the City Council struggling with this subject as well?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ statement.
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff –
 Regarding a department Mr. Jackson was speaking about earlier,
  what are they called again, and what is their tasks for the
  City?
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
 Wanted to know if our staff have worked with other Cities
  regarding the ADU and JADU in their Cities?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ statement.
 Do the lot areas have to be a certain size?
 Can HOA’s stop tenants from creating an ADU or JADU?
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Is there a possibility of restricting the bedroom sizes in an
  ADU or JADU unit? Can we also limit the number of bedrooms
  within the ADU, say two bedrooms as opposed to three rooms and
  for the JADU limiting it to one bedroom?
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 Can we require open space or a small grass area or patio area
  in the front – separating the buildings?
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 Since there are several other departments involved with ADU’s,
  possibly at the next Planning Commission meeting, those involved
  other departments would present to the Planning Commission and
  possibly answer some questions from us?
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the Commissioners if they had any further
questions or comments for staff.

There were none.

(8)  PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None, (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the hearings to the public and asked for
Planning Commission Initiatives.
